[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Hibernate Query Cache Configuration and Usage Tutorial"},{"order":2,"type":"subheading","text":"Introduction to the Query Cache"},{"order":3,"type":"paragraph","text":"The Hibernate Query Cache is an extension of the second-level cache. While the second-level cache stores entities by their identifier, the query cache stores result sets of queries. It maps parameter values to result sets containing entity identifiers, making it highly effective for read-heavy applications executing repetitive queries."},{"order":4,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 1: Enabling the Query Cache in Configuration"},{"order":5,"type":"paragraph","text":"By default, the query cache is disabled. To enable it, you must configure your persistence.xml or application.properties file to activate the second-level cache and the query cache property."},{"order":6,"type":"code","text":"<property name="hibernate.cache.use_second_level_cache" value="true"/>
<property name="hibernate.cache.use_query_cache" value="true"/>
<property name="hibernate.cache.region.factory_class" value="org.hibernate.cache.jcache.JCacheRegionFactory"/>"},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 2: Activating Caching on Specific Queries"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"Simply enabling the query cache globally is not enough. You must explicitly mark individual queries as cacheable in your Java code using the setCacheable(true) method."},{"order":9,"type":"code","text":"List<User> users = session.createQuery("FROM User u WHERE u.status = :status", User.class)
    .setParameter("status", "ACTIVE")
    .setCacheable(true)
    .getResultList();"},{"order":10,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 3: Understanding Query Cache Regions"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"By default, all cached queries are stored in a single region named org.hibernate.cache.spi.StandardQueryCache. However, you can assign queries to custom regions to fine-tune eviction policies and expiration times independently."},{"order":12,"type":"code","text":"List<User> users = session.createQuery("FROM User u", User.class)
    .setCacheable(true)
    .setCacheRegion("user-query-region")
    .getResultList();"},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices and Gotchas"},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Always ensure the entities returned by a cached query also have second-level caching enabled, otherwise Hibernate will execute a separate database query to fetch each entity identifier found in the query cache."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Avoid using the query cache for tables that undergo frequent updates, inserts, or deletes, as table modifications invalidate the entire query cache region, causing high overhead."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Monitor cache hit and miss ratios using your caching provider's metrics to confirm that your query cache configuration is actively improving application performance."}]
